papers.title: A Theory of Speciation in Generative Diffusion Models on Compact Riemannian Manifolds

reading.problem: Speciation in generative diffusion models denotes the emergence of distinct stable branches during denoising, through which initially undifferentiated trajectories progressively commit to different data classes.
reading.approach: In this work we develop an intrinsic theory of speciation for diffusion models supported on compact Riemannian manifolds: the aim is to go beyond existing theoretical descriptions, which usually identify speciation with a symmetric pitchfork bifurcation and assume to work in a large-dimensional space.
reading.evidence: We further establish structural stability of nondegenerate folds under score perturbations and show that the first-order time shift is determined solely by the component of the score error along the critical direction.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Speciation in generative diffusion models denotes the emergence of distinct stable branches during denoising, through which initially undifferentiated trajectories progressively commit to different data classes.

papers.title: Restoring Without Forgetting: Continual Learning Across Image Degradations

reading.problem: Recent progress in image restoration has converged on all-in-one architectures that jointly handle multiple degradations within a single network.
reading.approach: These methods are effective on static benchmarks but target a closed-world setting that assumes simultaneous access to every target degradation at training time.
reading.evidence: Across the five-domain sequence, RwF improves final average PSNR over naive sequential fine-tuning by 15.25 dB and 11.83 dB on the Restormer and NAFNet backbones, respectively.

papers.title: Graph-dependent shrinkage priors for Bayesian trend filtering

reading.problem: Many common data dependencies can be characterized by graphs: time series data are sequential (chain graph), images appear as pixels (lattice graph), areal data are defined by neighboring units (spatial adjacency graph), etc.
reading.approach: For the proposed graph-dependent shrinkage priors, we study the local concentration and adaptivity properties and establish conditions for posterior propriety.
reading.evidence: Simulation studies demonstrate that, relative to state-of-the-art frequentist and Bayesian alternatives, this framework provides more accurate point estimates, more precise interval estimates, and highly competitive computing.
reading.limitations: However, classical trend filtering only incorporates the graph for estimation of the trend, which limits its adaptivity, and is brittle in the presence of missing data.
reading.why_it_matters: Our approach leverages the graph at three critical junctures: 1) the trend, to enable smoothing, imputation, and prediction; 2) the local shrinkage, to enhance adaptivity and precision; and 3) the MCMC sampling algorithm, to deliver scalable posterior (predictive) inference via sparse and banded operations.

papers.title: LUCAID: Agentic Multimodal AI for Lung Cancer Precision Pathology

reading.problem: Lung cancer tissue diagnostics is complex, as therapy decisions in precision oncology rely on the integration of histomorphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular features.
reading.approach: To address these challenges, we developed and clinically validated LUCAID, an agentic AI system for precision lung cancer pathology.
reading.evidence: LUCAID enables users to interactively query the module outputs and generate reports that contextualize the results.
reading.limitations: Yet pathological assessment remains largely visual and semi-quantitative and shows interobserver variability, while existing artificial intelligence (AI) tools cover only selected tasks, rarely reach generalizable expert-level performance, and lack prospective clinical validation.
reading.why_it_matters: LUCAID enables users to interactively query the module outputs and generate reports that contextualize the results.

papers.title: Giga-Embeddings: Mixture-of-Experts Encoders for High-Throughput Text Embeddings

reading.problem: We introduce Giga-Embeddings, a family of text embedding models designed to combine strong retrieval quality with efficient serving.
reading.approach: Its largest member is a sparse 10B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts encoder with approximately 1.8B active parameters per token.
reading.evidence: Across English, Russian, multilingual, and code MTEB benchmarks, this model achieves the strongest aggregate performance within the family on all four evaluated suites.

papers.title: Serving Masked Diffusion LLMs: Characterization and Design Principles from Real Hardware

reading.problem: Masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) can in principle generate text faster than autoregressive (AR) models, since they denoise many tokens at once.
reading.approach: Recent systems have begun building serving infrastructure for dLLMs, but none first measure how these models behave under real, concurrent serving load.
reading.evidence: Batching mainly helps by amortizing this overhead: sharing one forward pass per denoising step improves throughput by 16.0x at batch size 16 over a per-request-dispatch baseline.

papers.title: Discovering Cross-Language Reasoning Invariance in LLMs with Geometry-Invariant Sparse Autoencoders

reading.problem: Multilingual language models can solve the same mathematical problem in different languages, but it remains unclear whether they rely on shared features or on language-specific computations that only produce similar outputs.
reading.approach: We study this question in five models from four families using the Multilingual Grade School Math (MGSM) dataset, with problems solved in English, German, French, Spanish, Russian, and Chinese, retaining problems with valid reasoning traces in all six languages and replaying those traces through the model to record representations at multiple layers.
reading.evidence: We then test whether the resulting shared features are functionally interchangeable by swapping their values between languages during the model's forward pass and measuring the resulting change in output, quantified by Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence per feature.
reading.limitations: Multilingual language models can solve the same mathematical problem in different languages, but it remains unclear whether they rely on shared features or on language-specific computations that only produce similar outputs.
reading.why_it_matters: GI-SAE primarily amplifies cross-language structure already present: the pattern is model-specific, with strengthening in Qwen, no functional benefit in Gemma, and mixed layer-dependent effects in Llama and Phi.

papers.title: Generating Biomedical Fact-Checking Reports with RL-Enhanced Agentic Search

reading.problem: Automated fact-checking is essential for ensuring the reliability of public health information, yet the biomedical domain poses unique challenges.
reading.approach: To bridge this gap, we introduce an LLM-based agent named BioCheck Agent that generates structured biomedical fact-checking reports with agentic search.
reading.evidence: Recognizing that direct prompting often results in hallucinations and low-quality reports, especially for lightweight open-source models, we further propose the Evidence-Grounded Group Relative Policy Optimization (EG-GRPO) to perform reinforcement learning on BioCheck Agent with a task-specific reward that incentivizes advanced search behavior and high-quality evidence retrieval while penalizing hallucinations.
reading.limitations: Automated fact-checking is essential for ensuring the reliability of public health information, yet the biomedical domain poses unique challenges.

papers.title: From Preferences to Principles: Rubric-Based Alignment for Grounded Knowledge Answers

reading.problem: Designing effective reward signals for open-domain question answering is challenging because high-quality responses must simultaneously satisfy multiple aspects of answer quality that are difficult to capture with a holistic scalar objective.
reading.approach: We introduce a rubric-based reward framework that generates query-specific rubrics grounded in retrieved evidence and decomposed into multiple quality dimensions, providing fine-grained supervision during post-training.
reading.evidence: Averaged across three evaluation axes (composition, grounding, and instruction-following), our approach improves over the instruction-tuned baseline by 6.5% and over flat rubric variants by 4%, with consistent gains across all evaluation datasets.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Designing effective reward signals for open-domain question answering is challenging because high-quality responses must simultaneously satisfy multiple aspects of answer quality that are difficult to capture with a holistic scalar objective.

papers.title: Learning to Grade Efficiently: A Bandit-Driven Prompt-Selection Framework for Low-Cost LLM Essay Scoring

reading.problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in automated essay scoring (AES), but contemporary approaches typically employ fixed prompt selection, failing to address operational cost concerns and evolving optimal configurations.
reading.approach: We propose a novel cost-aware approach that treats each prompt type as an arm in a multi-armed bandit (MAB) controller, enabling adaptive selection of optimal prompting strategies during inference.

papers.title: A Formal Methodological Framework for Auditing Robustness and Fidelity in Explainable AI: From Application to Trust Certification

reading.problem: SHAP and LIME are now standard tools for interpreting black-box predictions, yet their outputs can vary substantially when the input is perturbed by small amounts of noise--a problem we observed firsthand in our previous work on food security in Madagascar (Ralinirina et al., 2025).
reading.approach: This variability raises the question of whether such explanations can be trusted at all.
reading.evidence: The results are sobering: models with AUC above 0.99 can produce numerically degenerate or flatly uninformative explanations, and fidelity scores lose discriminative power when the model is overfitted.

papers.title: Place, Slice and Schedule: Hierarchical O-RAN Control of a Tethered mmWave UAV-gNB

reading.problem: LLM agents integrated with external resources gain complex task capabilities, yet the unified natural-language context channel makes them vulnerable to injection attacks: untrusted external data may be dynamically parsed as behavior-guiding instructions during LLM inference, thereby subverting the agent's decision.

papers.title: Beyond Confidence: Test-Time Scaling for Multi-Turn Search Agents via Retrieval Grounding

reading.problem: Confidence-based voting aggregates parallel LLM rollouts by weighting each with internal signals such as token log probabilities, and has been actively studied for single-turn reasoning.

reading.limitations: However, modern LLMs increasingly act as multi-turn search agents that retrieve and condition on external documents.

reading.problem: Endpoint-only unsupervised 4D medical image interpolation synthesizes intermediate volumes from sparsely sampled sequences with only the start and end volumes available for training; however, this weakly constrained setting often yields intermediates with unstable boundaries and non-physiological motion, limiting interpretability and downstream analysis.

reading.evidence: Experiments on ACDC and 4D-Lung demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, remaining competitive with methods trained with intermediate-frame supervision, and producing intermediates with improved structural coherence and more stable anatomical contours.

papers.title: Dataset Scarcity Limits Robust Evaluation of Multilingual Embedding Models: A Case Study of Slavic Languages

reading.problem: Multilingual text embedding models enable cross-lingual transfer of knowledge across a wide range of NLP tasks, but their evaluation remains highly uneven across high-, mid- and low-resource languages.
reading.approach: In this paper, we propose a two-dimensional framework, specifically tailored for analyzing multilingual embedding benchmarks under dataset scarcity, and apply it on the Slavic-language subset of the MTEB benchmark.
reading.evidence: Overall, the results demonstrate that benchmark rankings and robustness conclusions must be interpreted jointly with certain notation of their evidence strength and highlight benchmark scarcity as a major obstacle to trustworthy multilingual evaluation.
reading.limitations: Multilingual text embedding models enable cross-lingual transfer of knowledge across a wide range of NLP tasks, but their evaluation remains highly uneven across high-, mid- and low-resource languages.
reading.why_it_matters: Multilingual text embedding models enable cross-lingual transfer of knowledge across a wide range of NLP tasks, but their evaluation remains highly uneven across high-, mid- and low-resource languages.

papers.title: WarpSAC: Towards the Pinnacle of Scalable Off-policy RL by Rethinking Exploration and Exploitation

reading.problem: Massively parallel simulation changes the data regime in which off-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is trained, challenging stabilizers designed for data-limited replay.
reading.approach: Based on these findings, we propose WarpSAC, a regime-aware family of off-policy RL algorithms.
reading.evidence: Through controlled experiments across eight benchmark families, we show that these stabilizers are data-regime-dependent: parameter normalization helps with narrow replay coverage but restricts value fitting when data are abundant, while clipped double-Q can be relaxed in high-throughput manipulation.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Massively parallel simulation changes the data regime in which off-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is trained, challenging stabilizers designed for data-limited replay.

papers.title: On Scaling Coordinate-Based Neuroevolution: The Quadtree Bottleneck in ES-HyperNEAT

reading.problem: ES-HyperNEAT evolves substrate topology through adaptive quadtree subdivision; to our knowledge, no implementation with full population-level GPU parallelization exists.
reading.approach: We present JAX-ESHN, a JAX-based implementation targeting GPU parallelization with batched CPPN queries, and benchmark it against the CPU-based PUREPLES Baseline across five tasks: XOR, Parity-3, circle classification, sine regression, and CartPole.
reading.evidence: The abstract does not state a quantitative result.
reading.limitations: The core limitation is structural: each CPPN discovers a unique set of substrate positions, preventing population-level vectorization via vmap.
reading.why_it_matters: ES-HyperNEAT evolves substrate topology through adaptive quadtree subdivision; to our knowledge, no implementation with full population-level GPU parallelization exists.

papers.title: Beyond Static Interpretability: Anticipating Post-SFT Mechanisms from Pre-SFT Parameters for Better Tuning

reading.problem: Mechanistic Localization bridges mechanistic interpretability and post-training optimization by isolating critical parameters via interpretative approaches and then guiding parameter-efficient Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) in a ``locating-then-tuning'' paradigm.
reading.approach: To address this, we propose a forward-looking localization framework that accurately estimates the post-SFT interpretability state using only pre-SFT parameters and the target dataset.
reading.evidence: Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach not only provides superior SFT guidance but also exhibits robust performance and temporal scalability across increasing model sizes.
reading.limitations: However, due to the retrospective nature of mechanistic interpretability, directly interpreting pre-SFT models introduces misleading conclusions.
reading.why_it_matters: Practically, we design dual-granularity (neuron- and component-level) localization pipelines.

papers.title: NeuralParker: A Reinforcement Learning Planner for Irregular Parking Environments

reading.problem: Automated parking commonly assumes marked slots and short approach maneuvers.
reading.approach: To address this problem, we present NeuralParker, a reinforcement learning-based hybrid planner for arbitrary-pose parking.
reading.evidence: Experiments on these benchmarks show that NeuralParker achieves higher planning success and better overall trajectory quality than the evaluated baselines, while ablation studies support the benefits of the target-relative global representation and terminal ensemble.
reading.limitations: Delivery and service vehicles, however, may need to reach an operator-specified pose in an irregular bounded environment from a distant start.
reading.why_it_matters: Experiments on these benchmarks show that NeuralParker achieves higher planning success and better overall trajectory quality than the evaluated baselines, while ablation studies support the benefits of the target-relative global representation and terminal ensemble.

papers.title: Model Effect or Label Effect? Refined Annotations and a Human-Referenced Benchmark for Pulmonary Embolism Segmentation

reading.problem: Purpose: To quantify how evaluation annotations influence measured pulmonary embolism (PE) segmentation performance relative to model training changes, and to establish a human-referenced framework.
reading.approach: Materials and Methods: This retrospective study screened 166 voxel-annotated CT pulmonary angiography cases from CADPE (n=91), FUMPE (n=35), and READ (n=40); 149 were included.
reading.evidence: Results: Changing only the annotation increased mean DSC by 0.143 (0.122-0.166) for nnU-Net-A and 0.188 (0.163-0.213) for nnU-Net-B (both P < .001), whereas changing training-dataset composition changed DSC by 0.028.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Purpose: To quantify how evaluation annotations influence measured pulmonary embolism (PE) segmentation performance relative to model training changes, and to establish a human-referenced framework.

reading.problem: Many continuous-control policies are optimized as unbounded Gaussians and then mapped into bounded actions.
reading.approach: We show that where entropy is measured changes the policy geometry learned by proximal policy optimization (PPO).

papers.title: When Do Supervised UQ Ensembles Improve LLM Hallucination Detection? A Robustness Study

reading.problem: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods are widely used for hallucination detection in large language models (LLMs) in closed-book settings where ground-truth evidence is unavailable at inference time.
reading.approach: We study a supervised ensembling framework that trains a classifier over heterogeneous UQ-based scorer outputs on a small, domain-specific dataset of labeled LLM responses, then applies it to out-of-sample hallucination classification without retrieval, tools, or reference documents.
reading.evidence: We find that supervised ensembles outperform the best individual scorer in 30 of 32 settings, with gains realized from as few as 100 labeled instances.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Sampling-based black-box ensembles are nearly as effective as full ensembles, while single-generation white-box ensembles offer limited benefit.

papers.title: SeriCrypt: An LLM-Driven Context-Aware Serialization Framework for Cryptographic Protocols

reading.problem: Constructing syntactically correct and cryptographically valid message sequences is essential for protocol state machine learning, conformance testing, and fuzzing.
reading.approach: We present SeriCrypt, an LLM-driven, context-aware serialization framework for cryptographic protocols.

papers.title: PeakBench: Benchmarking Resource-Aware Tool Invocation in LLM Agents

reading.problem: LLM agents increasingly solve tasks by invoking multiple tools, where parallel execution is essential for low latency but difficult to manage safely.
reading.approach: To address this gap, we introduce PeakBench, a benchmark of executable multi-tool workflows with execution-grounded dependency annotations and measured resource profiles.
reading.evidence: Using this framework, we show that strong logical planning does not reliably translate into safe or efficient execution under resource constraints.
reading.limitations: A central challenge in evaluating such workflows is attribution: failures and inefficiencies may arise from incorrect dependency planning, poor resource-constrained scheduling, or both.
reading.why_it_matters: This missing scheduling dimension creates a practical failure mode: serial execution is safe but slow, while resource-agnostic parallel execution is fast but prone to avoidable resource overflows.

papers.title: SatDL: Jointly Optimizing Data Redistribution and Training for Satellite-Based Distributed Learning

reading.problem: Satellite-based distributed learning promises to train machine-learning models directly in orbit using massive, globally dispersed sensor data, thereby avoiding large-scale data downloads to ground servers.
reading.approach: We present SatDL, a data-redistribution framework designed to minimize total end-to-end learning time.
reading.evidence: Both extremes result in excessive total end-to-end learning time (data-transfer delay plus training time) and thus elevated onboard energy consumption.
reading.limitations: However, training convergence is significantly slowed by severe non-IID data, specifically label imbalance, as each satellite observes different geographic regions with distinct labels.
reading.why_it_matters: Satellite-based distributed learning promises to train machine-learning models directly in orbit using massive, globally dispersed sensor data, thereby avoiding large-scale data downloads to ground servers.

papers.title: It depends: Incorporating correlations for joint aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties of high-dimensional output spaces

reading.problem: Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) plays a vital role in enhancing the reliability of deep learning model predictions, especially in scenarios with high-dimensional output spaces.
reading.approach: We propose a novel approach that approximates the resulting joint uncertainty using a low-rank plus diagonal covariance structure, capturing essential output correlations while avoiding the computational burdens of full covariance matrices.

papers.title: Beyond Information Seeking: Severity-Aware Question Supervision for Proactive Medical Dialogue

reading.problem: Proactive medical dialogue requires an agent to decide what to ask from incomplete patient information.
reading.approach: To this end, we propose Expected-Severity-Risk (ESR), a consequence-aware question-supervision objective that values each candidate by its expected reduction in severity-aware terminal risk.
reading.evidence: Across three Qwen3-4B training seeds on DDxPlus, matched ESR supervision reduces mean high-severity diagnostic miss from .0645 to .0455 (-29.5%) and improves mean diagnostic accuracy from .9123 to .9320 while requiring only 0.14 additional questions per dialogue.
reading.limitations: Fixed-budget analyses show that the two objectives remain behaviorally distinct when question count is controlled, while a matched expected-0/1-risk control shows that severity-aware weighting improves the high-severity error profile beyond generic decision-aware supervision.
reading.why_it_matters: While effective for acquiring informative evidence, this criterion overlooks an important property of medical diagnosis: different diagnostic errors can carry substantially different consequences.

papers.title: LumiXAI: A Modular Full-Stack Framework for Feature Attribution

reading.problem: Feature attribution is a central tool of model interpretability, yet the software through which it is applied remains fragmented: individual tools specialize along narrow axes, such as a single modality, a code API or a GUI, or a fixed rather than extensible method set, and rarely combine these strengths.
reading.approach: In this article, we present LumiXAI, a modular full-stack framework that consolidates attribution analysis into a single system.
reading.evidence: Its contribution is a system that operationalises established attribution methods under one interface, one interaction model, and one persistence layer, with containerised services and persistent results making analyses reproducible across machines.
reading.limitations: Feature attribution is a central tool of model interpretability, yet the software through which it is applied remains fragmented: individual tools specialize along narrow axes, such as a single modality, a code API or a GUI, or a fixed rather than extensible method set, and rarely combine these strengths.

papers.title: RoG-DAgger: Rollout-Guided Post-Training for End-to-End Driving

reading.problem: Recent end-to-end driving systems demonstrate strong performance on closed-loop benchmarks, yet are still predominantly trained on fixed expert-collected data using open-loop imitation learning.
reading.approach: To address this, we introduce RoG-DAgger, a post-training framework that uses short-horizon kinematic rollouts to construct high-quality expert demonstrations in safety-critical states.
reading.evidence: Recent end-to-end driving systems demonstrate strong performance on closed-loop benchmarks, yet are still predominantly trained on fixed expert-collected data using open-loop imitation learning.
reading.limitations: Existing driving DAgger pipelines, however, face three challenges: i) the expert is restricted to a limited trajectory-and-speed solution space, ii) takeover may occur too early or too late relative to impending failures, and iii) privileged expert decisions may rely on information unavailable to the student.
reading.why_it_matters: Recent end-to-end driving systems demonstrate strong performance on closed-loop benchmarks, yet are still predominantly trained on fixed expert-collected data using open-loop imitation learning.

papers.title: Provable Quantum--Classical Separation for Continuous Gibbs Sampling

reading.problem: We prove the first quantum--classical separation for a sampling problem over a continuous domain.
reading.approach: For a class of Gibbs states $p\propto e^{-βE}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$ with smooth ($s$-Gevrey) potential and barrier amplitude $α=e^{βΔ}$, where $Δ= \max E-\min E$, every classical algorithm---querying the value, gradient, or any higher-order derivatives of the log-density---requires $Ω(α)$ queries to sample at constant accuracy in total variation distance, while a quantum algorithm based on quantum singular value thresholding and temperature annealing samples with $\tilde{O}\left(\sqrtα\right)$ queries to an oracle for the gradient.
reading.evidence: The abstract does not state a quantitative result.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: We prove the first quantum--classical separation for a sampling problem over a continuous domain.

papers.title: Persistent Cross Entropy

papers.title: Fiber Optic Sensing Glove for High Performance Dexterous Manipulation Capture

reading.problem: Capturing hand pose during dexterous manipulation remains difficult: vision-based methods degrade under occlusion and challenging lighting, while sensorized gloves, though occlusion-free, are prone to drift and magnetic interference and rarely match motion-capture accuracy.

papers.title: Lifted Model Construction under Approximate Commutativity

reading.problem: Lifted inference algorithms enable scalable probabilistic inference even for large object domains by leveraging the indistinguishability of objects in a probability distribution.

reading.problem: Hyperparameter selection remains a key challenge in Bayesian optimization (BO) and Bayesian active learning (AL), as model misspecification can lead to suboptimal performance, while more accurate fully Bayesian treatments typically rely on computationally expensive MCMC sampling.

reading.problem: Outcome-supervised search agents learn when and how to retrieve evidence, but terminal rewards neither localize intermediate errors nor redirect an ongoing trajectory before those errors compound.
reading.approach: We introduce CAFE (Coupled Agent--Feedback Evolution), a framework in which a shared-parameter model alternates between search-agent and critic roles.
reading.evidence: Treating corrective feedback as a learned in-trajectory intervention couples the two roles: the agent must decide when to request and use feedback, while the critic must infer useful corrections from outcome-confounded rollouts whose failure patterns shift as the agent improves.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Outcome-supervised search agents learn when and how to retrieve evidence, but terminal rewards neither localize intermediate errors nor redirect an ongoing trajectory before those errors compound.

papers.title: LION: A Clifford Neural Paradigm for Multimodal-Attributed Graph Learning

reading.problem: Recently, the rapid advancement of multimodal domains has driven a data-centric paradigm shift in graph ML, transitioning from text-attributed to multimodal-attributed graphs.
reading.approach: Despite its promise, limitations exist in the current neural paradigms:(1) Neglect Context in Modality Alignment: Most existing methods adopt topology-constrained or modality-specific operators as tokenizers.These aligners inevitably neglect graph context and inhibit modality interaction, resulting in suboptimal alignment.(2) Lack of Adaptation in Modality Fusion: Most existing methods are simple adaptations for 2-modality graphs and fail to adequately exploit aligned tokens equipped with topology priors during fusion, leading to poor generalizability and performance degradation.To address the above issues, we propose LION (c\underline{LI}ff\underline{O}rd \underline{N}eural paradigm) based on the Clifford algebra and decoupled graph neural paradigm (i.e., propagation-then-aggregation) to implement alignment-then-fusion in multimodal-attributed graphs.
reading.evidence: Despite its promise, limitations exist in the current neural paradigms:(1) Neglect Context in Modality Alignment: Most existing methods adopt topology-constrained or modality-specific operators as tokenizers.These aligners inevitably neglect graph context and inhibit modality interaction, resulting in suboptimal alignment.(2) Lack of Adaptation in Modality Fusion: Most existing methods are simple adaptations for 2-modality graphs and fail to adequately exploit aligned tokens equipped with topology priors during fusion, leading to poor generalizability and performance degradation.To address the above issues, we propose LION (c\underline{LI}ff\underline{O}rd \underline{N}eural paradigm) based on the Clifford algebra and decoupled graph neural paradigm (i.e., propagation-then-aggregation) to implement alignment-then-fusion in multimodal-attributed graphs.
reading.limitations: Despite its promise, limitations exist in the current neural paradigms:(1) Neglect Context in Modality Alignment: Most existing methods adopt topology-constrained or modality-specific operators as tokenizers.These aligners inevitably neglect graph context and inhibit modality interaction, resulting in suboptimal alignment.(2) Lack of Adaptation in Modality Fusion: Most existing methods are simple adaptations for 2-modality graphs and fail to adequately exploit aligned tokens equipped with topology priors during fusion, leading to poor generalizability and performance degradation.To address the above issues, we propose LION (c\underline{LI}ff\underline{O}rd \underline{N}eural paradigm) based on the Clifford algebra and decoupled graph neural paradigm (i.e., propagation-then-aggregation) to implement alignment-then-fusion in multimodal-attributed graphs.
reading.why_it_matters: This advancement significantly enhances data representation and expands the scope of graph downstream tasks, such as modality-oriented tasks, thereby improving the practical utility of graph ML.

papers.title: StarHarness: Evolving Harnesses with Stratified Search for Enterprise Environments

reading.problem: We present StarHarness, a framework for evolving environment-specific agent harnesses while keeping model weights fixed.
reading.approach: The evolved harness can include prompt and task framing, tool interfaces, skills, MCP-backed providers, subagent structure, and agent-loop configuration.
reading.evidence: Across ITBench SRE, EnterpriseOps-Gym ITSM, and AutomationBench Finance, harness evolution improves full-benchmark performance by 20-35 percentage points over the default harness after 4-12 accepted changes per environment.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: StarHarness therefore offers a practical way to reduce persistent model-environment mismatch in tool-rich enterprise tasks.

papers.title: Automatic Model Card Generation Using an LLM

reading.problem: Model cards are structured documents that summarize key information about machine learning models to improve transparency, usability, and accountability.
reading.approach: First, we propose MCTidy, an LLM-based approach that reorganizes existing model cards into a standardized template to improve clarity and comparability.
reading.evidence: Model cards are structured documents that summarize key information about machine learning models to improve transparency, usability, and accountability.
reading.limitations: However, they often lack a consistent structure, and many models provide no model cards, making comparison and interpretation difficult.
reading.why_it_matters: Overall, our findings demonstrate the potential of LLM-based methods to enable scalable, standardized model card documentation.

papers.title: Structurally-bounded Agentic Graph Exploration for Evidence-Grounded Scholarly DeepSearch

reading.problem: We present Crase, a bounded and inspectable alternative to deep research agents for scholarly search.
reading.approach: Instead of an open-ended search loop, Crase queries a search engine once for seed papers, expands them along their 1.5-hop citation neighborhood, prunes citation edges whose claims lack entailment support, and ranks the remaining papers with a recency-aware random walk.
reading.evidence: On LitSearch and one further benchmarks over a 500K-paper arXiv corpus, Crase outperforms deep research agents built on proprietary models by up to 3$\times$ recall@50 at roughly a third of the cost.
reading.limitations: Instead of an open-ended search loop, Crase queries a search engine once for seed papers, expands them along their 1.5-hop citation neighborhood, prunes citation edges whose claims lack entailment support, and ranks the remaining papers with a recency-aware random walk.
reading.why_it_matters: We present Crase, a bounded and inspectable alternative to deep research agents for scholarly search.

papers.title: Strictly Causal Streaming Video Anomaly Detection with a Theoretically-Grounded State-Space Core

reading.problem: Recent work has applied Mamba style state space models (SSMs) to video anomaly detection, yet existing approaches still rely on buffering clips or windows internally, lack a theoretical account of how temporal memory relates to detection latency, and benchmark efficiency only through GPU throughput rather than the edge hardware these methods are intended to target.
reading.approach: We introduce a strictly causal streaming anomaly detector whose fixed size state is updated in O(1) time and memory per incoming frame, with no lookahead and no clip buffering.
reading.evidence: The abstract does not state a quantitative result.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Recent work has applied Mamba style state space models (SSMs) to video anomaly detection, yet existing approaches still rely on buffering clips or windows internally, lack a theoretical account of how temporal memory relates to detection latency, and benchmark efficiency only through GPU throughput rather than the edge hardware these methods are intended to target.

papers.title: MDTE: Minority-Aware Diffusion over Temporal Edge Events for Imbalanced Node Classification

reading.problem: Class-imbalanced node classification on temporal graphs is challenging because majority-dominated temporal propagation progressively assimilates minority representations, while conventional node and neighborhood information provides insufficient discriminative evidence for minority classes.
reading.approach: To address these issues, we propose MDTE, a minority-aware diffusion framework that reconstructs stable and discriminative temporal edge-event representations through conditional diffusion denoising.
reading.evidence: Experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that MDTE consistently achieves the best performance on minority-class-oriented metrics, improving minority-class recall by up to 23.53 percentage points, minority-class F1 by 8.68 percentage points, and AUPRC by 2.67 percentage points over the strongest baselines.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Class-imbalanced node classification on temporal graphs is challenging because majority-dominated temporal propagation progressively assimilates minority representations, while conventional node and neighborhood information provides insufficient discriminative evidence for minority classes.

papers.title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining

reading.problem: We uncover ELR collapse in language model pretraining: learning rate (LR) and parameter norm govern loss dynamics primarily through their ratio, the effective learning rate (ELR).
reading.approach: When ELR is matched across runs, their loss trajectories collapse throughout training despite substantially different LRs and parameter norms.
reading.evidence: Controlled interventions further show that weight decay and Hyperball shape loss dynamics primarily through the ELR schedules they induce.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Replacing LR with ELR enables a fitted functional scaling law (FSL) to transfer across norm-control methods.

papers.title: A Geometric Theory of Robust Fairness Audits

reading.problem: Neighborhood-based fairness audits evaluate individual fairness by comparing predictions among similar individuals in feature space.
reading.approach: We develop a geometric framework for analyzing the robustness of neighborhood-based fairness audits under bounded perturbations.
reading.evidence: Experiments on benchmark datasets support the theoretical analysis and show that the proposed framework explains the observed stability of neighborhood-based fairness audits.
reading.limitations: Because these audits rely on nearest neighbor relationships, small perturbations in feature space can alter local neighborhoods and produce different fairness assessments even when model predictions remain unchanged.
reading.why_it_matters: Neighborhood-based fairness audits evaluate individual fairness by comparing predictions among similar individuals in feature space.

papers.title: BioKERN: Biological Kernel Regularization for Histology-to-Transcriptomics Neighborhood Retrieval

reading.problem: Spatially resolved biology requires representations that preserve biological neighborhood structure rather than only exact cross-modal correspondences.
reading.approach: We introduce BioKERN, a multimodal spatial representation-learning framework that incorporates biological structure as an explicit, learnable inductive bias.
reading.evidence: Across Mouse Brain Visium and Human Liver GSE240429, BioKERN consistently improves biological-neighborhood retrieval over BLEEP in both single- and multi-scale settings.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Spatially resolved biology requires representations that preserve biological neighborhood structure rather than only exact cross-modal correspondences.

papers.title: Constrained Entity Selection under Partial Knowledge for LLM-Based Knowledge Graph QA

reading.problem: Large language models are increasingly used for knowledge graph question answering (KGQA), but can fail to correctly ground answers in the underlying graph.
reading.approach: In this work, we study a complementary setting in which \emph{candidate} answers are generated by an LLM-based system and subsequently verified using lightweight symbolic constraints derived from the question.
reading.evidence: To demonstrate the effects of our method, we instantiate this framework over the Hetionet biomedical knowledge graph and evaluate the impact of type, relation, and exclusion constraints.
reading.limitations: Satisfied constraints provide additional positive symbolic evidence to rank remaining candidates.
reading.why_it_matters: Large language models are increasingly used for knowledge graph question answering (KGQA), but can fail to correctly ground answers in the underlying graph.

papers.title: A Dual-Dimensional LLM Framework for Automated Item Incidental Content Similarity Analysis in Large-Scale Assessments

reading.problem: The rapid expansion of large-scale assessments and the growing adoption of automatic item generation have intensified concerns about incidental content redundancy, where construct-irrelevant elements such as wording or contextual framing become unintentionally repetitive across items.
reading.approach: Traditional similarity metrics like BLEU or cosine similarity, often fail to capture the nuanced structural and semantic layers that drive perceived redundancy simultaneously.
reading.evidence: Simulations reveal that incorporating LLM-based similarity constraints into item selection improves estimation stability and reduces bias with minimal efficiency trade-offs, outperforming constraints based on conventional metrics.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: The rapid expansion of large-scale assessments and the growing adoption of automatic item generation have intensified concerns about incidental content redundancy, where construct-irrelevant elements such as wording or contextual framing become unintentionally repetitive across items.

papers.title: Reading Is Not Using: Retrieval, Judgment, and the Design of AI Financial Research Workflows

reading.problem: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as AI analysts to process financial disclosures and support AI-assisted investment decisions.
reading.approach: Yet such systems are usually evaluated by what they can retrieve, not whether retrieved information affects their judgments.
reading.evidence: Causal memory interventions show that compressed summaries and source-text lookup jointly transmit disclosures into judgments.
reading.limitations: Holding focal-firm information fixed and varying only unrelated context from 2,000 to 128,000 tokens, we find that a risk disclosure's influence on investment judgments falls to the experimental noise floor even as direct retrieval remains accurate.
reading.why_it_matters: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as AI analysts to process financial disclosures and support AI-assisted investment decisions.

papers.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training

reading.problem: We present LAION-BVD, a large-scale open video dataset for multimodal learning, which contains 1.3B platform-specific video URLs collected from CommonCrawl.
reading.approach: From these, we download 80M videos with a total duration of 10 million hours.
reading.evidence: Models trained on these data achieve competitive performance on standard video-text and audio-text benchmarks, with consistent improvements as training or model scale increases.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: We present LAION-BVD, a large-scale open video dataset for multimodal learning, which contains 1.3B platform-specific video URLs collected from CommonCrawl.

papers.title: FedV-KGQA: Multi-Hop Question Answering over Vertically Partitioned Knowledge Graphs

reading.problem: Real-world data for knowledge graph question answering is often distributed across different organizations due to governance and data sovereignty constraints.
reading.approach: In this paper, we propose FedV-KGQA, a framework for multi-hop reasoning over knowledge graphs in which organizations share entities but own disjoint sets of relations.
reading.evidence: We evaluate 12 model configurations across three benchmarks and show that FedV-KGQA performs strongly, remains close to centralized performance, generalizes to 3-hop reasoning, and is robust to embedding perturbations.
reading.limitations: We evaluate 12 model configurations across three benchmarks and show that FedV-KGQA performs strongly, remains close to centralized performance, generalizes to 3-hop reasoning, and is robust to embedding perturbations.
reading.why_it_matters: Real-world data for knowledge graph question answering is often distributed across different organizations due to governance and data sovereignty constraints.

papers.title: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes

reading.problem: Web agents that act from rendered pixels avoid the fragility and heavy token cost of reading a page's HTML or accessibility tree, but training them depends on large amounts of high-quality interaction trajectories, and how to produce such data at scale remains an open problem.
reading.approach: We present BrowserForge, a framework that generates web interaction data at scale by driving many browser sandboxes in parallel over the open web.
reading.evidence: The resulting corpus contains 203,238 trajectories, each collected from a distinct website, larger and more diverse than prior trajectory datasets.
reading.limitations: Web agents that act from rendered pixels avoid the fragility and heavy token cost of reading a page's HTML or accessibility tree, but training them depends on large amounts of high-quality interaction trajectories, and how to produce such data at scale remains an open problem.
reading.why_it_matters: Web agents that act from rendered pixels avoid the fragility and heavy token cost of reading a page's HTML or accessibility tree, but training them depends on large amounts of high-quality interaction trajectories, and how to produce such data at scale remains an open problem.

papers.title: Learning Whom to Trust : Decision-Generated Credibility in Social Learning

reading.problem: Social interaction can improve collective learning but also amplify early mistakes.
reading.approach: We study this tension when the credibility of social information is generated by the sender's own decision process rather than fixed ex ante.
reading.evidence: Social interaction can improve collective learning but also amplify early mistakes.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Social interaction can improve collective learning but also amplify early mistakes.

papers.title: LeFlow: Generative Latent Flow Planning for World Models

reading.problem: Latent world models are inherently strong encoders that transform image pixel to latent embedding, yet existing world models still rely on online trajectory optimization for action planning: for every state-goal pair, an iterative optimizer is run from scratch to search for optimal action sequences, treating the world model as a black-box simulator.
reading.approach: We present LeFlow, which learns a reusable latent trajectory prior operating directly in the latent dynamics space from the world model.
reading.evidence: Our results argue that latent world models should support not only prediction but reusable planning priors.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Latent world models are inherently strong encoders that transform image pixel to latent embedding, yet existing world models still rely on online trajectory optimization for action planning: for every state-goal pair, an iterative optimizer is run from scratch to search for optimal action sequences, treating the world model as a black-box simulator.

papers.title: Bellman Calibration for Marginalized Importance Weighting in Offline Reinforcement Learning

reading.problem: Marginalized importance weighting evaluates a target policy by reweighting offline state-action samples with its discounted occupancy ratio, characterized by an adjoint Bellman equation.
reading.approach: We introduce isotonic Bellman calibration, a one-dimensional, model-agnostic post-processing method that reduces these violations while preserving the ranking information in any initial occupancy-ratio estimate.
reading.evidence: Consequently, isotonic Bellman calibration achieves small calibration error and KL risk within statistical error of the best monotone correction, with guarantees for downstream target-occupancy functionals, including policy-value estimation.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Marginalized importance weighting evaluates a target policy by reweighting offline state-action samples with its discounted occupancy ratio, characterized by an adjoint Bellman equation.

papers.title: Improving Cross-Problem Vehicle Routing with Locally Augmented Preferences and Representation Disentanglement

reading.problem: Multi-task vehicle routing problem (VRP) solvers seek to handle multiple VRP variants within a single unified model, avoiding the need to train a separate model for every variant.
reading.approach: First, we propose Preference Optimization with Locally Augmented Refinement (POLAR), a novel training algorithm that applies a local search refinement pass to the best decoded tour before forming preference pairs, yielding much more informative pairwise margins.
reading.evidence: On the training side, reinforcement learning suffers from reward-scale disparities and shrinking advantage signals as policies improve, whereas preference optimization stagnates once sampled tours become near-identical and thus fundamentally limited by the quality of the policy's own generated solutions, leaving both paradigms with weak supervision as training progresses.
reading.limitations: In spite of recent progress, current approaches remain limited on two fronts.
reading.why_it_matters: Multi-task vehicle routing problem (VRP) solvers seek to handle multiple VRP variants within a single unified model, avoiding the need to train a separate model for every variant.

papers.title: Parameterized Complexity of $L_p$-Lipschitz Constants for Input Convex Neural Networks and $L_p$-Norm Maximization over Zonotopes

reading.problem: Lipschitz constants are a standard way to quantify the sensitivity of neural networks to small input perturbations, but computing them is difficult even for shallow ReLU networks.
reading.approach: We study this problem for two-layer input-convex neural networks (ICNNs), a restricted architecture where nonnegative output weights enforce convexity.
reading.evidence: Moreover, our hardness results imply that brute-force enumeration algorithms are essentially optimal for this problem under the Exponential Time Hypothesis.
reading.limitations: While $L_1$- and $L_\infty$-norm maximization on zonotopes admit fixed-parameter and polynomial-time algorithms, respectively, the parameterized complexity of the remaining $L_p$-norms was open.
reading.why_it_matters: Lipschitz constants are a standard way to quantify the sensitivity of neural networks to small input perturbations, but computing them is difficult even for shallow ReLU networks.

papers.title: SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL

reading.problem: Group-relative reinforcement learning waits for sibling rollouts of the same prompt, which is costly for long and variable tool-use trajectories.
reading.approach: Single-stream Policy Optimization (SPO) removes this dependency with a persistent prompt-level value estimate, but its recipe whitens one advantage per trajectory before optimizing a token-mean actor loss.
reading.evidence: We show that trajectory centering generally does not center the token-weighted quantity consumed by the actor, and fix the mismatch by standardizing terminal-outcome advantages under the action-token measure.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Group-relative reinforcement learning waits for sibling rollouts of the same prompt, which is costly for long and variable tool-use trajectories.

papers.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses

reading.problem: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) remains hard in long-horizon tasks, where growing histories obscure the task state and misalign skill invocation.
reading.approach: We introduce Recuris, a recursive Experiential-Working Memory architecture for long-horizon agent harnesses, in which Working Memory tracks task progress and guides skill selection from Experiential Memory, grounding skill use in current needs rather than the full history.
reading.evidence: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) remains hard in long-horizon tasks, where growing histories obscure the task state and misalign skill invocation.
reading.limitations: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) remains hard in long-horizon tasks, where growing histories obscure the task state and misalign skill invocation.
reading.why_it_matters: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) remains hard in long-horizon tasks, where growing histories obscure the task state and misalign skill invocation.

papers.title: From Seeing to Acting: Smart Glasses as First-Person Intelligence Platforms

reading.problem: Smart glasses are evolving from capture and display accessories into first-person intelligence platforms that connect human perception, persistent context, and digital or physical action.
reading.approach: Their on-body viewpoint aligns with the wearer's vision, audition, motion, and hand-object interaction, but must operate under tight energy, thermal, privacy, and feedback constraints.
reading.evidence: The abstract does not state a quantitative result.
reading.limitations: Despite rapid progress in augmented reality, egocentric vision, multimodal models, human-computer interaction, and embodied intelligence, the literature remains fragmented across devices, tasks, and benchmarks. \textit{The key challenge is not whether a model can recognize, answer, remember, or act in isolation, but whether a complete system can sustain a reliable, temporally valid, correctable, and governable perception-state-interaction-action loop.} This survey is \textit{the \textbf{first} to systematically study smart glasses through such a unified framework}.
reading.why_it_matters: Smart glasses are evolving from capture and display accessories into first-person intelligence platforms that connect human perception, persistent context, and digital or physical action.

papers.title: What FID Hides: Detecting, Ranking, and Diagnosing Deviations in Generative Evaluation

reading.problem: Generative models are commonly ranked by Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Kernel Inception Distance (KID), yet FID's first-two-moment summary can miss distributional differences, and a reported scalar gap alone is not a calibrated test against sampling variation.
reading.approach: We introduce \textbf{ZID} (\emph{Z-resolved Integrated Diagnostic}), which combines six standardized location- and dispersion-sensitive arms from a rank graph (RISE) and Gaussian kernels (GPK at two bandwidths).
reading.evidence: The abstract does not state a quantitative result.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Generative models are commonly ranked by Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Kernel Inception Distance (KID), yet FID's first-two-moment summary can miss distributional differences, and a reported scalar gap alone is not a calibrated test against sampling variation.

papers.title: Latent Action as Intention Enables Efficient Future Imagination for World Action Models

reading.problem: World action models (WAMs) improve robot control by modeling how observations evolve, but generating future observations at test time incurs substantial latency.
reading.approach: To bridge this gap, we introduce **LAWA**, a WAM architecture that uses compact latent actions as an operational representation of future intentions, enabling efficient test-time future imagination without generating future observations.
reading.evidence: World action models (WAMs) improve robot control by modeling how observations evolve, but generating future observations at test time incurs substantial latency.
reading.limitations: Fast-WAM removes this process for efficiency; however, our matched implementations show lower generalization for Fast-WAM than for future-aware alternatives, especially with scarce robot demonstrations and in out-of-distribution scenarios.
reading.why_it_matters: World action models (WAMs) improve robot control by modeling how observations evolve, but generating future observations at test time incurs substantial latency.

papers.title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning

reading.problem: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly used as learned simulators for policy evaluation and improvement, yet their effectiveness rests on an unverified assumption: generated futures faithfully reflect arbitrary valid actions.
reading.approach: To address this gap, we introduce WorldEcho, which probes action following over a broader action distribution using visual integrity and SE(3) trajectory alignment.
reading.evidence: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly used as learned simulators for policy evaluation and improvement, yet their effectiveness rests on an unverified assumption: generated futures faithfully reflect arbitrary valid actions.
reading.limitations: The abstract does not report limitations; verify them in the full paper.
reading.why_it_matters: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly used as learned simulators for policy evaluation and improvement, yet their effectiveness rests on an unverified assumption: generated futures faithfully reflect arbitrary valid actions.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.

Most cells are low-dimensional synthetic sweeps over noise, sample size, and capacity. Multi-seed grids and one frozen latent-diffusion confirmation are material but far cheaper than training a modern image generator.

The primary supports expose true score, projection, topology, component mass, density, and volume. Every proposed cheap norm is evaluated prospectively against distinct, preregistered recovery endpoints.

Low-noise score singularity, manifold rates, finite-sample convergence, gradient-versus-solenoidal error, and geometry-aware training already exist. Novelty is the finite-noise cross-support audit and explicit no-universal-norm result, not another asymptotic bound.
Circle, torus, and disconnected-support pilots can separate raw L2, gradient-projected, high-quantile, and covering-grid errors within days; boundary and latent-transfer claims take longer.

assumptions: Population convolved scores and nearest-support projections can be computed analytically or to audited numerical tolerance for the primary low-dimensional support families.

A finite covering grid and adaptive adversarial residual search approximate the relevant uniform error closely enough to serve as an oracle diagnostic, while remaining clearly labeled unavailable in natural data.
Score networks can be trained across enough independent datasets and initializations to distinguish sample, optimization, and support-class variance.
The natural latent-space confirmation is a transfer check only and cannot validate unknown topology or manifold truth.

brief.title: Which score error buys which geometry? A finite-noise norm-gap audit
brief.thesis: Train score models on known connected, disconnected, boundary, and stratified supports across finite noise, sample size, capacity, and optimization budgets. Compare held-out denoising L2, the gradient component of score error, local high-quantile residuals, normal-versus-tangential residuals, and an oracle covering-grid sup error. Freeze a predictor on development supports and ask which observable signal forecasts tubular concentration, Hausdorff support error, topology, component weights, density, uniform-volume recovery, and sampler mixing on unseen support classes. Permit the correct result to be that no single norm orders all targets.
brief.motivation: Geometry-first score theory separates an order-sigma^-2 normal confinement term from order-one density structure, but its guarantees use asymptotic uniform error on a compact smooth manifold rather than an observable training loss. Covariance-based denoiser approximations show that simple statistics can explain part of a score field; statistic-learning work shows higher-order structure can emerge only later; and memorization studies show forward-noised training probes can diverge from actual reverse-trajectory states. Most importantly, current theory shows raw L2 score error can be arbitrarily large while the target marginal remains exact because solenoidal error is invisible to Fokker-Planck marginals. The missing bridge is a prospective finite-noise audit that distinguishes recovery targets and tests gradient-projected and local alternatives rather than assuming training risk transfers to geometry.
brief.research_question: Across finite sample, noise, capacity, and support regimes, which observable components of learned-score error prospectively predict support geometry, topology, component mass, density, and mixing—and when is any scalar norm provably or empirically non-ordering?
non_claims: The project does not claim the first manifold diffusion theorem, score decomposition, finite-sample bound, topology metric, or geometry-aware sampler.
Raw denoising L2 is not assumed to be monotone in marginal distribution quality or any geometric endpoint.
Support concentration, Hausdorff recovery, topology, curvature, density recovery, uniform-volume exploration, and fast mixing are separate outcomes.
Uniform manifold volume is a changed target, not a more accurate estimate of a nonuniform data distribution.
A low-dimensional synthetic phase diagram does not certify the unknown manifold of natural images or a production latent diffusion model.
subquestions: Does the gradient component estimated through a dual Sobolev identity predict marginal density while normal high-quantile error better predicts support concentration?
At what finite sigma and sample size do the asymptotic normal-versus-tangential error classes become visible, if at all?
Can two models with matched denoising L2 have different topology, component-mass, or mixing outcomes, and which residual diagnostic forecasts the split?
How do boundaries, intersections, density zeros, disconnected components, curvature, reach, and changing intrinsic dimension alter the ranking of norms?
Does a predictor frozen on analytic supports retain calibration on an unseen support generator and one latent diffusion checkpoint family?
method: Create audited support families with analytic or high-precision numerical convolved scores: circles, spheres, tori, curves with controlled reach, unequal disconnected components, intervals and disks with boundary, intersecting or stratified unions, and distributions with registered density zeros or bottlenecks.

Cross noise level, sample size, ambient and intrinsic dimension, network width/depth, training steps, and dataset resampling. Train standard denoising score matching models across at least eight seeds per primary cell and retain full checkpoint trajectories rather than selecting only best loss.

On disjoint forward-noised validation samples and reverse-trajectory states, measure standard L2, gradient-projected error through the dual Sobolev estimator, solenoidal residual, local 90th/99th-percentile error, Jacobian and curl diagnostics, oracle normal and tangential residuals, and adaptive covering-grid L-infinity error.

Sample with matched reverse SDE, probability-flow ODE, Langevin corrector, and tempered-score variants. Equalize score evaluations and discretization error so sampler differences cannot masquerade as learned-score geometry.

Evaluate tubular mass, Hausdorff and Chamfer support error, projection error, persistent-homology barcodes and Betti numbers, curvature and reach where identifiable, connected-component mass, on-support Wasserstein or KL density error, uniform-volume error, low-density bridges, hitting time, and effective mixing.

Fit sparse, monotone only where justified, uncertainty-calibrated maps from predeclared error features to each endpoint on development supports. Freeze features, thresholds, coefficients, and abstention rules before opening a support class with different boundary or topology.

After the synthetic audit, freeze one diagnostic panel and test a small latent diffusion family across checkpoints and noise levels using empirical neighborhood, held-out-density, memorization, and trajectory-shift proxies. Make no unobservable natural-manifold claim.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: This is a finite-noise calibration study, not a universal scaling law. Freeze the metric panel and response maps before changing support class, dimension, or latent model; report where calibration fails rather than fitting a new exponent after the fact.
supporting_evidence: On untouched support classes, one or more observable error components predict their registered recovery target with calibrated uncertainty beyond denoising L2, elapsed compute, and capacity alone.
Matched-L2 model pairs exhibit prospectively predicted differences in topology, component mass, density, or mixing, demonstrating why target-specific diagnostics matter.
Normal and tangential or gradient and solenoidal interventions produce the predicted selective endpoint changes at fixed total error magnitude.
Finite-noise response surfaces approach the asymptotic ordering only in identifiable regimes and abstain elsewhere.
The frozen panel directionally predicts held-out latent-model trajectory or memorization outcomes without selecting checkpoints on the final metric.
claim_blockers: No error feature improves held-out prediction beyond noise, sample size, capacity, and training step.
The gradient-projected or local metrics are too noisy to calibrate without using the target support oracle at test time.
Matched-L2 pairs do not yield stable endpoint differences or the result reverses across seeds and discretizations.
Persistent-homology and component-mass results are artifacts of sample count, neighborhood bandwidth, or sampler budget.
The frozen predictor requires support-specific threshold or exponent refitting.
The latent confirmation reverses the registered direction or ordinary trajectory-shift baselines dominate.
prospective_design: Develop metrics on circles, spheres, and one connected curved support; reserve disconnected, boundary, and stratified families.
Freeze noise grid, sample and capacity cells, seed count, sampler budgets, topology estimators, error features, and all abstention rules.
Open one unseen support family at a time and never recalibrate the primary predictor on its outcomes.
Freeze the final panel again before the latent diffusion check and publish all target-specific failures, not an aggregate success score.
why_small_models_fail: Low-dimensional oracles expose projection, normal bundles, topology, and density that are unknown in natural representations.
A fixed smooth support omits learned encoders, semantic conditioning, nonstationarity, and changing latent dimension.
Finite-grid uniform error is exponentially costly with dimension and cannot become a practical large-model validator unchanged.
Reverse diffusion is time-inhomogeneous, while fixed-noise Langevin stationary behavior can conceal discretization and trajectory-distribution effects.
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Claim a target-specific finite-noise calibration only for support families and dimensions that pass untouched evaluation. If no observable norm generalizes, publish the non-ordering counterexamples and reject a universal geometry-first training certificate.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A frozen target-specific model using gradient-projected and local high-quantile score residuals will predict held-out support, topology, component-mass, and density error more accurately than denoising L2, training step, noise level, or capacity alone on unseen support classes.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: Normal and tangential or gradient and solenoidal error interventions with matched total L2 will selectively change geometric versus marginal outcomes, creating preregistered matched-L2 counterexamples to a universal scalar ordering.
domains: Analytic connected circles, spheres, tori, and curved manifolds with controlled reach and curvature
Unequal disconnected components and narrow-bottleneck supports
Intervals, disks, manifolds with boundary, intersections, and stratified unions
One frozen low-dimensional latent diffusion checkpoint family as an external-validity check
baselines: Held-out denoising L2, train loss, training step, network capacity, and sample size
Gradient-component dual Sobolev estimate, solenoidal component, curl, local high-quantile residual, and adaptive sup-error oracle
Normal-only, tangential-only, gradient-only, solenoidal-only, random, and norm-matched injected score errors
Reverse SDE, probability-flow ODE, standard corrector, and tempered-score corrector at equal score evaluations
Raw sample quality, nearest-training distance, forward-probe gap, reverse-trajectory gap, and covariance-only denoiser predictors
ablations: Remove gradient projection, high-quantile error, normal-tangential decomposition, or trajectory-state measurements
Use forward-noised validation states only versus actual reverse-trajectory states
Hold total L2 fixed while rotating error among gradient, solenoidal, normal, and tangential components
Connected versus disconnected support and equal versus unequal component weights
Smooth closed support versus boundary, intersection, density-zero, and stratified cases
Equal sampler steps versus converged or extrapolated mixing estimates
experiment.primary_outcome: Held-out calibration and rank prediction for each preregistered recovery endpoint—support Hausdorff error, topology error, component-mass error, on-support density error, and mixing time—on unseen support families.
experiment.analysis: Use dataset draw and training seed as crossed random effects; compare nested frozen predictors with out-of-support-family log score, rank correlation, calibration slope, and interval coverage. Test matched-L2 interventions as randomized contrasts, correct the fixed endpoint family for multiplicity, and model censored non-mixing runs rather than dropping them. Report no aggregate winner when different norms govern different targets.
experiment.decision_rule: Pass only target by target: the frozen observable panel must improve prediction over L2 and resource baselines with calibrated intervals on every registered holdout of that target, and matched-L2 component interventions must change the predicted endpoint selectively. If calibration requires oracle support access, post hoc thresholding, or support-specific refitting, reject the practical certificate.

falsifiers: Denoising L2 and simple resource variables match every richer observable on held-out support families.
Gradient-projected, high-quantile, or trajectory-state metrics cannot be estimated with useful variance from finite validation data.
Norm-matched component interventions fail to produce target-selective changes.
Topology or component recovery changes only with sampler discretization or sample count, not the registered error component.
The asymptotic sigma ordering does not appear anywhere in the finite-noise regime studied.
The frozen latent-space check reverses the diagnostic ranking.
evaluation: Held-out denoising L2, gradient-projected Sobolev error, solenoidal residual, curl, Jacobian spectrum, high-quantile error, normal and tangential error, and adaptive grid sup error
Tubular concentration, projection distance, Hausdorff and Chamfer support distance, coverage, and low-density bridge rate
Persistent-homology bottleneck distance, Betti-number error, component discovery, curvature, reach, boundary, and intersection recovery
Component-mass calibration, on-support Wasserstein and KL error, uniform-volume discrepancy, and density-zero leakage
Reverse-SDE and ODE error, sampler discretization, hitting time, autocorrelation, effective sample size, and censored mixing time
Checkpoint, samples, parameters, FLOPs, wall time, score evaluations, dataset seed, initialization seed, and uncertainty calibration
Latent forward-probe versus reverse-trajectory error, memorization gap, nearest-training distance, and held-out sample-distribution metrics
risks: Numerical score or projection oracles can be wrong on stratified supports. Validate against analytic special cases, refine quadrature and covers until tolerance is stable, and publish residual bounds.

A finite cover can miss narrow sup-error spikes. Combine deterministic covers, gradient-based adversarial residual search, and Lipschitz envelopes, while labeling it an oracle diagnostic rather than a scalable metric.
Persistent homology is sensitive to sample count and bandwidth. Match samples, use bootstrap barcodes and analytic topology, and report failure to resolve short-lived features.
Injected error fields may violate learned-network structure. Compare analytic interventions with naturally trained matched-L2 checkpoints and treat agreement as a separate gate.
Endpoint proliferation invites selective synthesis. Freeze five primary endpoints and allow different metrics—or none—to win each one.
Latent natural data lack geometric ground truth. Restrict transfer claims to observable trajectory and distribution metrics and do not back-infer topology.
first_week: Implement analytic circle, sphere, torus, and two-component mixture scores across a finite noise grid and verify them by automatic differentiation and quadrature.
Train eight seeds of one small score MLP over sample-size and width cells with checkpoint-complete logging.
Implement raw L2, dual-Sobolev gradient error, curl or solenoidal diagnostics, normal-tangential oracle error, high quantiles, and adaptive residual search.
Run equal-budget reverse SDE and Langevin sampling and compute support, component-mass, density, topology, and mixing outcomes.
Construct matched-total-error gradient-versus-solenoidal and normal-versus-tangential interventions, then preregister all holdouts and target-specific pass rules.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Models Observe Only Gradients: A Geometric Perspective on Score Matching Errors
competitive_landscape.difference: Khelifa et al. prove raw L2 score error cannot monotonically lower-bound marginal divergence, decompose gradient and solenoidal error, and propose a dual-Sobolev estimator. The audit makes that estimator a required baseline and tests additional support, topology, component, and mixing outcomes at finite noise.

competitive_landscape.title: Generalization Properties of Score-matching Diffusion Models for Intrinsically Low-dimensional Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Chakraborty et al. give finite-sample Wasserstein-p convergence governed by a generalized intrinsic dimension without manifold smoothness. The proposal empirically separates geometry, topology, density, and mixing rather than using one distributional endpoint.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Model for Manifold Data: Score Decomposition, Curvature, and Statistical Complexity
competitive_landscape.relationship: current manifold score and rate theory
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. decompose manifold scores, expose curvature dependence, and derive approximation and statistical rates. The audit tests which of those theoretically meaningful components can be estimated and calibrated across misspecified boundary and stratified supports.

competitive_landscape.title: Mathematical Analysis of Singularities in the Diffusion Model under the Submanifold Assumption
competitive_landscape.difference: Lu, Wang, and Bal characterize the normal score singularity near a manifold. The proposal turns asymptotic structure into finite-noise, finite-sample prediction tasks and includes supports that violate the smooth closed-manifold assumption.

competitive_landscape.title: Convergence of Diffusion Models under the Manifold Hypothesis in High-Dimensions
competitive_landscape.difference: Azangulov et al. provide intrinsic-dimension-sensitive score and sampling rates. Their assumptions and distributional targets become a theory baseline; the audit checks topology, components, boundaries, and observable norm calibration separately.

competitive_landscape.title: Convergence of Denoising Diffusion Models under the Manifold Hypothesis
competitive_landscape.difference: This work gives foundational convergence guarantees under manifold structure. The proposed study stresses finite-noise diagnostics and explicit assumption violations rather than adding another broad convergence theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving the Euclidean Diffusion Generation of Manifold Data by Mitigating Score Function Singularity
competitive_landscape.difference: Niso and Tango modify training using normal and tangential score structure. They are direct method baselines; the audit asks which measured component predicts each endpoint before recommending an objective.

competitive_landscape.title: Resolving Memorization in Empirical Diffusion Model for Manifold Data in High-Dimensional Spaces
competitive_landscape.difference: Lyu et al. analyze empirical-distribution memorization and introduce an inertial update with finite-sample bounds. The proposed phase diagram includes dataset resampling and nearest-training behavior but focuses on norm-to-target calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Models under Low-Noise Regime
